quote: Found a lovely lily (Calochortus albus) in a shady adenostoma thicket near Coulterville, in company with Adiantum Chilense.
author: John Muir
source: My First Summer in the Sierra

quote: We saw a splendid yellow lily by the shore, which I plucked.
author: Henry David Thoreau

quote: The adaptations for cross-fertilisation are perhaps more obvious in the Orchideae than in any other group of plants, but it is an error to speak of them, as some authors have done, as an exceptional case.
author: Charles Darwin
source: The Effects of Cross and Self-Fertilisation in the Vegetable Kingdom

quote: The risk of false impregnation by foreign pollen is, however, a very slight one with Pisum, and is quite incapable of disturbing the general result.
author: Gregor Mendel

quote: I never tire of admiring and praising Iris stylosa, which has proved itself such a good plant for English gardens; at any rate, for those in our southern counties.
author: Gertrude Jekyll

quote: In the hyacinth the bulbels form at the base of the bulb.
author: Liberty Hyde Bailey

quote: Orange trees were in full bloom, and filled the air with fragrance.
author: William Bartram

quote: The peanut exerts a dietetic or a medicinal effect upon the human system that is very desirable.
author: George Washington Carver

quote: The study of the violet will naturally bring about a review of the pansy; the dandelion, of the sunflower; the horse, of the donkey; the butterfly, of the moth.
author: Anna Botsford Comstock

quote: It is needless to eulogize the Rose.
author: Francis Parkman

quote: I have seen oaks of many species in many kinds of exposure and soil, but those of Kentucky excel in grandeur all I had ever before beheld.
author: John Muir
source: A Thousand-Mile Walk to the Gulf

quote: The trees are mostly oaks, planted wide apart like those in the Wisconsin woods.
author: John Muir
source: A Thousand-Mile Walk to the Gulf

quote: The sugar maple was the dominant tree in the woods and the maple sugar the principal sweetening used in the family.
author: John Burroughs

quote: Maple, beech, and birch wood kept us warm in winter, and pine and hemlock timber made from trees that grew in the deeper valleys formed the roofs and the walls of the houses.
author: John Burroughs

quote: Much green fern still in many places, although it is no longer erect.
author: Susan Fenimore Cooper

quote: Neither the holly, the cedar, the arbor vitæ, the cypress, or the laurel, grows in our immediate neighborhood, so that we are limited to the pine and hemlock.
author: Susan Fenimore Cooper

quote: The greater number are pines, and a more fitting tree for a Christian church-yard than the white pine of America could scarcely be named.
author: Susan Fenimore Cooper

quote: In the midst of this spot stood, in old times, a vast oak, with a short squat body, and huge horizontal arms extending almost to the extremity of the area.
author: Gilbert White

quote: The India-rubber fig penetrates thus far amongst the mountains, but is of small size.
author: Joseph Dalton Hooker

quote: The case of three or more cotyledons, which is constant in Pines and in some of their relatives (but not in all of them), is occasional among Dicotyls.
author: Asa Gray
